messages:
alex_support: FYI customer 'ScaleApps' opened a high-sev ticket — getting persistent 429s & token-level throttling on their Dedicated pool since ~08:05 UTC. They report tail latency spikes too. I checked dashboard and saw a bunch of requests routed to a 'shared' pool. Can oncall triage?

oncall_bob: Looking. Any request IDs or example traces from the customer?

alex_support: They pasted a request id: req_9f2b3c. Also included a curl: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-...\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate\" -d '{"model":"redwood-dedicated/gold-v2","input":"hi"}'` -> 429.

maya_infra: I pulled the routing logs for req_9f2b3c: shows policy match: `selector: tier=gold` but placement returned `pool: shared-small-1` with throttle=true. That is wrong.

runtime_sre: Repro on our side: sent 100 concurrent requests pinned to customer-id X via their API key, observed ~15% routed to shared pool and those hit a rate-limiter. Running full traces now.

maya_infra: Dump from control-plane cache at 08:03: `policy_map[customerX.tier] = \"dedicated-gold-pool\"` but at 08:05 the placement service returned fallback `shared-small-1` with reason: \"tier mismatch\".

eng_platform_lead_sam: @maya_infra can you paste config for the new routing service (v2.3.1) — we shipped a patch yesterday for pool selector improvements. Might be a regression.

maya_infra: Snippet of selector rules (redacted):
```
- name: choose_pool
n  match: req.labels.tier == \"Gold\"  # note capitalization
  pool: dedicated-gold
- name: fallback
  match: true
  pool: shared-small-1
```

maya_infra: The customer tier tag is `gold` (lowercase). Looks like the new matching logic became case-sensitive, so gold != Gold -> fallback.

oncall_bob: That would explain wrong pool selection and unintended throttling. Can we revert v2.3.1 quick or patch match logic?

eng_platform_lead_sam: I'm rolling a hotfix to normalize tags to lowercase in the placement service. Rolling back is heavier because it touched config stores. I'll push a patch and post the deploy ID.

deploy_bot: deploy started by sam (eng-platform) — deploy_id: dply-2024-08-28-67b9, target: placement-service v2.3.2-hotfix

maya_infra: Patch diff: `labels = [l.lower() for l in labels]` + unit tests. Also adding a short-circuit that prevents fallback for explicit tier pins if quota exists.

runtime_sre: After staging patch, re-ran repro load — 0% routed to shared pool, latency stable. Customer verified temporary success after we applied the change to staging.

billing_jane: Heads up: the customer flagged unexpected billing spikes when requests were retried during 429 loop. Need to calculate overcharged tokens window and coordinate credits.

cs_oliver: I told ScaleApps we'll keep them updated and offered credits for the impacted window. Please send me the final time range and reason so I can close the ticket.

maya_infra: Timeline: 08:01 UTC routing config rollout v2.3.1, 08:03 first mismatches started, 08:05 majority of their traffic hit fallback and throttled, mitigated by hotfix deploy at 08:22, full normalization at 08:24.

oncall_bob: Marking incident; raising a postmortem. Initial cause: control-plane routing matching became case-sensitive in v2.3.1 causing tier mismatch and incorrect pool selection -> unintended throttling on shared pool. Secondary impact: billing due to retries.

eng_platform_lead_sam: Action items: 1) add robust normalization tests for label matching (maya). 2) Add canary/traffic simulation for Dedicated tier pins in future rollouts (runtime_sre). 3) Prepare billing reconciliation script and customer credit proposal (billing_jane). 4) Update runbook to check pool selection logs quickly (alex_support).

billing_jane: I'll generate a provisional credit estimate by EOD and loop in finance.

cs_oliver: I'll send a customer-friendly summary and ETA for credits now that we have timeline.

alex_support: Thanks team. I'll update the support ticket with the timeline and link to this thread.

runtime_sre: Leaving a note: also observed a small race in placement cache TTL causing transient stale maps — we'll audit for other case-sensitive selectors.

eng_platform_lead_sam: Good catch. We'll include that in the postmortem. Closing the loop once credits are issued. :white_check_mark:
